summary: @servicetitan/error-boundary preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: Package advertises itself as a React error boundary implementation but ships a preinstall hook (setup.mjs, invoked via package.json scripts.preinstall) that downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases and uses it (or a local bun on PATH) to execute a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~728 KB heavily obfuscated JavaScript file (string-array rotation via WV8StW, hex-mangled identifiers such as MmgoCP/etDiOOB) whose filename does not match its content and which is not referenced from the package's TypeScript React error-boundary source. The actual React error boundary code shipped in dist/ is tiny (dist/index.js is 68 bytes, dist/error-boundary.js is ~2.9 KB) and unrelated to the install-time payload. Fetching a separate language runtime at install time to execute an obfuscated sibling script has no legitimate purpose for a React error boundary library and results in arbitrary attacker-controlled code executing under the installer's identity on npm install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
